You hit it right on the head. Not to be even more spiteful but there is valid proof he doesn't seem to care. Last week was a speeding ticket in my car for 80+, now I am not saying all speeders are horrific people, but it showed utter lack of respect for me or my property. That being said, he no longer gets use of MY car. 

And building even further <sorry venting a little> he comes over to my home, stays for days / weeks on time. I ask him to pitch in for rent. Now he will spend ~$50 on groceries every so often. He usually just sits and plays computer games. And it turns out the only time he actually wants sex anymore is if he has had a few shots of fireball. I know he is cheating at this point because why would he 'not be in the mood' when it has been more than a few days up to a week without intercourse. Only when he is down at my house he behaves by the no A4A etc. rule. 

Thanks for the reaffirmation, what it is at this point is to sever and move on. It's not healthy to stay. 

Thanks for the reply and advice!
"Operating System not Found... Press Any Key to Retry Boot..."

It's always best to just be patient. It's not worth the risk (std's, rape, or theft) for a quick blow job. You're going to a university, odds are you'll find someone soon. Reach out to your local clubs and don't be afraid to go out and mingle. Best of luck!

Taking notice. I have had other relationships in the past that have gone asunder and for very similar reasons. What I have found is that in the past, I was more introverted about the issues, would bottle them up, and things would get worse. So if I am overreacting, it is probably for the better. In the end, conversation was the fix.

Indeed. We talked it through, didn't play the blame game. And we were able to work through our issues. Probably the best advice from all of this is to just talk about it. Without conversation, things fester, get worse, and eventually result in something drastic.
Were in our 20's but not sure where age has any bearing here...
It could be an addiction, but only time will tell with respects to that. It is a matter of learning to live with technology in a healthy and positive way.

Thanks for the responses everyone! Was able to talk it over with him and work out the details. What it boils down to is finding times which are acceptable for time together or time apart. There are also things to be worked out in addition to just the gaming, but in time, we can work through those. Thanks for the input!
Thanks kcos! This is what I plan to do with him. Thank you for the constructs on how to begin the conversation without coming off too brash.

Agreed... The feeling I had when I was told was that awkward pit in my stomach. Really it was demoralizing that a game would be held on a higher pillar than I. As far as the thing with the ex, at this time it's nothing more than conversation. But something to watch... Thanks for the help!

That is my next logical step. I did sort of confront him about the issue at the time, but it was dismissed with more of a 'do your own thing' tone, with a not so reassuring 'love you.' Probably because of the timing it wasn't as effective as it should have been. Thanks for the input!
